findings.description: The new regex captures only the first find root, and deleting the root-count check allows multiple-root commands to inherit that root's allow-list classification.
findings.failure_mode: A command such as `find ./build / -exec rm -rf {} +` passes the hook because ./build is allowed, although find also invokes recursive deletion against /. The previous ambiguity check rejected this command.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore rejection of multiple or ambiguous roots, or parse and validate every find root before allowing the rm invocation.

findings.description: Both response paths now classify billing-related HTTP 400 errors as terminal InvalidInputError instead of ProviderUnavailableError.
findings.failure_mode: When the Anthropic account runs out of credits, requests terminate instead of walking the configured fallback chain to claude-headless. This removes the existing recovery behavior for an account-side outage.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve billing-error classification in both streaming and non-streaming paths so those failures continue to raise ProviderUnavailableError.

findings.description: Completed sprint counting now includes historical directories, while the total still counts only the current sprint plan.
findings.failure_mode: With one unfinished sprint in the current plan and one historical sprint directory containing COMPLETED, determine_state reports complete, skips checking the unfinished sprint, and recommends /deploy-production.
findings.suggested_fix: Count completion markers only for sprints belonging to the current plan, using the same sprint identities and scope as the total and state checks.

findings.description: The new `_re_find_exec_prefix` captures only find's FIRST non-space token as group 3 and the per-token loop that enforced exactly one root (`_find_root_count -ne 1` -> root cleared) was deleted. `_seg_find_root` is now set unconditionally from BASH_REMATCH[3]. For `find ./build / -exec rm -rf {} +` or `find ./tmp "$HOME" -exec rm -rf {} +` the hook resolves the rm against `./build` and never inspects `/` or `$HOME`. Base behavior cleared the root on multi-root spans and fell through to the conservative block.
findings.failure_mode: A destructive recursive rm whose find command lists an allow-listed first root and a protected second root exits 0 (allowed) on head where base exits 2 (blocked). This is a safety-hook bypass with real deletion impact.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the single-token capture but re-add the span check: capture the full span (`([^;&|)]*)-exec$`) as before and only accept it when exactly one non-flag token precedes the first `-`/`!`/`(`/`\\` token; otherwise set `_seg_find_root=""`. Add fixtures for two-root and `-L`-prefixed find commands.

findings.description: The comment claims `find -L root -exec ...` 'keeps today's conservative behavior', but it does not: base broke the token loop on `-*` and left `_seg_find_root` empty; head captures the literal `-L` (or `-H`, `-P`, `-O2`) as the root string. Whether downstream root classification treats a bare `-L` as a relative, allow-listed path cannot be confirmed from the diff, but the behavior is new, undocumented in fixtures, and not conservative.
findings.failure_mode: If the root classifier treats an unknown relative token as a cwd-relative allowed path, `find -L / -exec rm -rf {} +` is misclassified using `-L` instead of `/`.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude leading-dash tokens from group 3 (e.g. `([^-;&|)[:space:]][^;&|)[:space:]]*)`) so flag-first invocations fall back to empty root, or extend the regex to skip `-[HLP]`/`-O` flags before the root. Correct the comment either way.

findings.description: Deleting `_is_billing_class_error` and both call sites (streaming path at 139-141, non-streaming path at 223) collapses every non-401/403/429 4xx into `InvalidInputError`. Anthropic returns billing conditions (credit balance exhausted, quota exceeded, invoice overdue) as HTTP 400 with an account-side message; these are not request-side failures and were deliberately routed to `ProviderUnavailableError` so the chain walker could fail over to the next provider (cycle-109 #883 Bug 3).
findings.failure_mode: On a billing-exhausted account every call is terminal with 'Anthropic API error (HTTP 400)'; the provider chain never falls over to the configured fallback, so the whole pipeline fails instead of degrading. This is a regression of a fixed bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore `_BILLING_CLASS_TOKENS` / `_is_billing_class_error` and the two `ProviderUnavailableError` branches, or move the classification into a shared helper if the intent was deduplication. Do not change the raised exception type.

findings.cross_file_justification: .claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_adapter_billing_class.py imports `_is_billing_class_error` from the diff-touched module and asserts `ProviderUnavailableError` on billing-class 400s; the diff removes the symbol and the behavior without touching the test.
findings.description: The module-level symbol `_is_billing_class_error` is removed but a test module still imports it by name. Python raises ImportError at collection time, which fails the entire test module (not just the billing assertions) and, depending on the runner config, the whole adapter test session.
findings.failure_mode: `pytest .claude/adapters/tests` errors during collection with `ImportError: cannot import name '_is_billing_class_error'`; CI red, and any other tests in that module are silently not run.
findings.suggested_fix: Either restore the symbol (preferred, per DISS-003) or delete/rewrite the test module in the same change. Never remove an imported public-to-tests helper without updating its consumers.

findings.description: The rewrite counts every `a2a/sprint-*` directory with a COMPLETED marker, regardless of the current sprint.md total. The base implementation (and its R-004/bd-m1o6 comment) was explicitly scoped to `1..get_total_sprints()` because archive-cycle copies a2a but never removes it, and ledger-lib numbers a2a dirs by global id, so historical COMPLETED dirs accumulate across cycles. `determine_state` does `completed >= total && total > 0 -> STATE_COMPLETE`, and `get_progress_percentage` computes `completed*70/total`.
findings.failure_mode: On any project past its first cycle, a freshly planned sprint.md with N sprints and zero work done reports state=complete, progress 95%, suggested_command=/deploy-production, and `completed_sprints` > `total_sprints` in --json. loa-status and the SessionStart surface mislead the operator and skip the implement/review/audit phases. This is exactly the regression R-004 fixed.
findings.suggested_fix: Revert to iterating `1..$(get_total_sprints)` and checking `${a2a_dir}/sprint-${i}/COMPLETED`, or if global-id numbering is the concern, resolve the current cycle's sprint ids via the ledger (`.cycles[] | select(.id==$active_cycle) | .sprints[].global_id`) and count COMPLETED only for those. Keep the R-004 comment.

findings.description: `for dir in ${sprint_dirs}` word-splits the newline-separated find output on IFS (space/tab/newline). If PROJECT_ROOT or the grimoire dir contains a space, each path fragments and `[[ -f "${dir}/COMPLETED" ]]` is false for every piece.
findings.failure_mode: Projects checked out under a path with spaces always report 0 completed sprints, so state never advances past implementing.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `while IFS= read -r -d '' dir; do ...; done < <(find "${a2a_dir}" -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'sprint-*' -print0 2>/dev/null)` or a `for dir in "${a2a_dir}"/sprint-*/` glob with `nullglob`. Moot if DISS-005 is fixed by reverting to the numeric loop.
